literal: If one does harmful things to others in the forenoon, harmful things will come to themselves in the afternoon on their own.
translation: If you do evil to others in the morning, evil will come to you on its own in the afternoon.
modern: ஒருவர் மற்றவருக்குக் காலையில் துன்பம் செய்தால், அவருக்குத் துன்பமானது மாலையிலேயே தானாக வந்து சேரும்.
explanation: This couplet uses the natural division of a single day to illustrate the swift and inevitable return of one's actions. The terms 'முற்பகல்' (forenoon) and 'பிற்பகல்' (afternoon) serve as metaphors for the early and later stages of life, or simply the rapid cycle of cause and effect. The poet emphasizes that the harm we inflict on others ('பிறர்க்கு இன்னா') does not go unanswered; it returns to us ('தமக்கு இன்னா') automatically ('தாமே வரும்') without needing any external agent to deliver the punishment.
